messages:
noah_sales: Zenith Corp POC hit an auth wall during demo. They see 401s then a few 403s when switching test projects. Can we swarm?
zenith_eng: Quick summary: using hosted endpoint, bearer token from onboarding email. Local calls succeed but CI runners behind company VPN get 401 Invalid API key. Sometimes when we flip project header it becomes 403.
rachel_se: Thx. Two likely culprits: (1) the key is bound to a different org/project than the one your CI is sending; (2) proxy or CI injects `X-RWD-Org-Id` / `X-RWD-Project-Id`. Can you paste the curl you ran and any response headers?
zenith_eng: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/inference -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"hello"}'`
Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`
Body: `{"error":"Invalid API key"}`
Response headers included `x-rwd-request-id: rwd-req-0a7b9`
sam_platform: Pulling logs with the request id... (checking).
ops_bot: secrets-service: lookup rwd-req-0a7b9 -> key fingerprint found, status: active, bound_org: org-zenith-prod, bound_project: web-poc.
zenith_eng: Our CI env uses `RWD_PROJECT=zenith-test` (we leaked it from another repo). We didn't think the SDK would attach that.
rachel_se: The SDK will attach env org/project if present which overrides token binding. If the values don't match the key binding you'll get 403 Forbidden. 401 usually means the key was disabled/rotated or the token is malformed. With mixed runners some requests hit different envs/keys which explains the flip.
zenith_eng: Ok we removed RWD_PROJECT from the runners and retried. Still got a 401 from one runner.
ops_bot: secrets-service: recent audit shows one runner used a different key id (`rwd-old_4c3`) that was rotated earlier -> status: disabled at 2026-02-03T09:20:11Z. That explains the 401.
sam_platform: So two issues: env leak causing project mismatch and a stale rotated key slipped into one runner. Quick unblock: we can (A) generate a short-lived CI key scoped to inference-only for zenith-test, or (B) update all runners to remove stray envs and rotate keys. Which do you want?
zenith_eng: For immediate demo unblock create a temp key please. We'll clean CI setup afterwards.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: created key `rwd-test_zenith_ci_99`, bound_org: org-zenith-test, bound_project: zenith-test, scopes: [inference:generate], expires: 72h, status: active. id: rwd-test_zenith_ci_99.
zenith_eng: Key swapped into CI vars and reran -> all runners return 200 now. Thanks!
rachel_se: Two follow-ups for docs/security: 1) Can you confirm whether PoC keys can be scoped to embeddings-only and have IP restrictions?
sam_platform: Hosted PoC keys can be scope-limited (embeddings-only, inference-only) and TTL-limited. Per-key IP allowlisting (CIDR) is available for Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted public tier doesn't support per-key IP restrictions. We can mention short-lived service keys as a mitigation for hosted PoCs.
zenith_eng: Security ok with scoped short-lived keys. Another thing: we observed intermittent 429s when running concurrent embedding batches at ~120 rpm. Suggestions?
rachel_se: For embeddings batching: chunk into 8-16 items, use async concurrency control to keep per-client concurrency low, and implement exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s. Start at 4000 req/min per runner and ramp slowly while observing `x-rwd-remaining` and `x-rwd-reset` headers.
sam_platform: Also adding two product/UX asks: (1) show key binding (org/project) and last rotation timestamp next to keys in console, (2) SDK should warn in logs when env-provided org/project doesn't match token binding. I'll file small tickets.
ops_bot: crm: PoC ZEN-2026-45 updated: attached key rwd-test_zenith_ci_99, notes: env leak -> removed RWD_PROJECT, stale key rotated, rate guidance attached.
noah_sales: Great work team. Zenith, we'll link the PoC runbook with the key id and the CI checklist. Please ping here if anything else pops up. Closing the swarm. :white_check_mark:
